chapter: Billy Pierce Studio and New York tap
title: Billy Pierce discovering Buddy Bradley
summary: The woman interviewer explains how Billy Pierce gave Bradley his first teaching chance with Irene Delroy and so started the studio's fame among white performers.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What was the relationship with -- between Billy Pierce and Buddy Bradley?
Well now, that was a teacher and employer, you see. It was the Billy Pierce Studio --

Billy Pierce gave Buddy his first opportunity to teach. He had this idea of so many of the white performers needing this sort of rhythm dancing, and he gave Buddy his first opportunity with -- somebody, Irene Delroy -- she was in a show, in the Greenwich Village Follies, something like that. I hope I'm right.

And he asked Buddy -- Buddy, I think he was about 18 at the time -- if he thinks he could put a number together for Irene Delroy, which he did. He'd never done it before, but he just had this gift of making a girl look very cute with taps, without looking sort of hefty or awkward. And he taught her this little number, and she went back into the show, stopped the show, and that's what caused the influx of white show biz peoples at that time going to the Billy Pierce Studios and everybody wanting these hit numbers that stopped shows, naturally.
So that's really what started the fame of the Billy
